# Compacted Summary: Chapters 1-15 (Extended v122)

## Setting and Time
Multiple periods spanning French Revolution to 1826. **Current narrative point (Autumn Year 4, evening—crisis escalating at Gorbeau house)**: Paris—Gorbeau house (50-52, Salpêtrière district); Luxembourg gardens; le Petit-Picpus convent; M. Gillenormand's residences; English provincial towns (Dunstead, Staveford, Kelmere, Torton, Ostcombe, Ravenmere, Kelford, Yarlby, Gulhaven, Wilwick, Wilholt). **Current environmental**: Smoke from chimneys lies flat over fields, bell for vespers rings thinly across roofs, light went early, icy breeze, frost silvering hedges overnight, wind off water carries salt/tar scent, gulls quarrel over fish heads, rain threatens, road all ruts and puddles after thaw, someone chalked crooked sun on forge wall.

## Primary Locations
**GORBEAU HOUSE**: 50-52 Salpêtrière district. **JONDRETTE DEN**: Abject, fetid, sordid. Furniture: straw chair, infirm table, crockery, two pallets, straw beds. Walls: leprous, seamed, obscene charcoal sketches, repulsive moisture. Fireplace with brazier filled burning charcoal (glowing hot, red with blue flame), pot, broken boards, suspended rags, bird-cage. Dormer window (four broken panes). Colored engraving "THE DREAM" (sleeping woman/child, eagle, Napoleon on blue column). **Wooden panel—Battle of Waterloo painting: sergeant rescuer (Thénardier) carrying colonel victim (Pontmercy) amid smoke. Marius recognized father; Waterloo cannon sounds in ears.** Two heaps: old iron/ropes and rope-ladder with wooden rungs and two hooks. Verdigris candlestick with burning candle.

**Current state (evening, crisis escalating)**: M. Leblanc seized moment, overturned chair and table, moved toward window with prodigious agility. Six robust fists seized him—three "chimney-builders" dragged him back. Thénardier woman wound hands in his hair. Herculean struggle: M. Leblanc knocked old man tumbling, overthrew two more with backward hand sweeps, held one under each knee. Four others seized him by both arms and back of neck, holding him doubled up—M. Leblanc now beneath horrible group of ruffians like wild boar beneath howling pack of dogs.

**M. Leblanc bound with ropes.** Despite binding, surrounded, half plunged in grave, M. Leblanc remained impassive—soul inaccessible to terror, not knowing despair. Preserved silence, carried precaution of forgetting anxiety for own life. **Marius found this superbly melancholy visage and extraordinary composure deeply troubling, affected him with painful astonishment.**

## Thénardier's Metamorphosis and Negotiation (Evening Crisis)

**Nature**: Contains two men—ferocious and adroit. M. Leblanc's resistance calmed rather than exasperated him. **Now adopting polished, measured demeanor**: Rose unpretending manner, went to fireplace. **Marius found it difficult recognizing in that polished smile of man in official life the almost bestial mouth foaming moment before; felt as if witnessing tiger converted into lawyer.** Language now moderated, subdued, crafty, reserved, almost choice. In that rascal, formerly mere robber, one felt "the man who had studied for the priesthood."

**Current negotiation**: Thénardier stated: "We can come to understanding. Let us arrange amicably. I was wrong to lose temper just now... I don't want to ruin you. I'm not a greedy fellow. I'm taking things into consideration and making sacrifice on my side. I only want two hundred thousand francs."

**Thénardier's scheme**: Wife will dress as before and hunt up "the Lark" (the young girl) with letter from M. Leblanc. Girl will follow without difficulty into carriage. Outside barrier, trap with two good horses waits. Young lady will alight from fiacre; Thénardier's comrade will enter other vehicle with her; wife returns here to report completion. **Thénardier's threat**: "If you have me arrested, my comrade will give a turn of his thumb to the Lark, that's all." **Deliberate omission of name**: Thénardier avoided naming girl, said "the Lark," "the little one," but not her name—precaution of clever man guarding secret from accomplices.

**Girl's identity clarification**: Marius discovered: handkerchief bore letters U. F., which meant Urbain Fabre, not Ursule. M. Leblanc (Monsieur Fabre) is the girl's father. When Thénardier said "the Lark," prisoner replied naturally: "I do not know what you mean."

**M. Leblanc's address demanded**: Thénardier instructed M. Leblanc to write letter addressed "Mademoiselle Fabre" to his house. "I know that you live a long distance from here, near Saint-Jacques-du-Haut-Pas, because you go to mass there every day, but I don't know in what street. I see that you understand your situation. As you have not lied about your name, you will not lie about your address. Write it yourself."

## Jean Valjean and Cosette
Valjean integrated as convent assistant gardener; inhabits old garden hut with Fauchelevent. Spiritual transformation complete. Cosette became convent scholar; believes Valjean is her father; adores him. Fauchelevent sole ally aware of full presence. **Present state (Autumn Year 4)**: Cosette about thirteen/fourteen years old; appeared in Jondrette hovel as charitable visitor with M. Leblanc (her biological father). **Marius now recognizes**: The "girl" he worshipped for six months is Cosette, whom he encountered again miraculously in the hovel; she is also being held captive by Thénardier's scheme.

## Javert's Pursuit
Attached to Paris police. **Status (Autumn Year 4)**: Tall man, square face, thin firm mouth, thick gray ferocious whiskers. **Action (present, evening)**: Received report from Marius regarding Jondrette ambush. Gave Marius two small steel pistols (each loaded two balls). Instructed Marius to hide, watch through wall hole, fire when crisis reached peak. Entered hovel, purchased chisel, positioned himself for ambush. Gave key to Marius.

## Marius Pontmercy: Development, Passion, and Crisis

**Identity and age**: Baron Marius Pontmercy, twenty years old; three years estranged from grandfather. **Paternal legacy**: Colonel's written instruction regarding baron title and Waterloo sergeant Thénardier. Lost medallion of black shagreen. **Now recognized**: Thénardier depicted in Waterloo painting—sergeant who rescued father at Waterloo.

**Girl (Cosette)—Passion and rediscovery**: Marius noticed man approximately sixty (M. Leblanc) and very young girl on Luxembourg bench daily over six months, year prior. Girl: thin, awkward, convent scholar dress. Six-month interruption. Reunion (Summer Year 3): Girl became well-dressed young maiden; wore black damask dress, white crape bonnet, white gloves, carved Chinese ivory parasol handle, silken shoe. **First meaningful glance (Spring Year 4)**: Their glances met. Marius resolved to dress differently. Perceived she wore everyday clothes. His worship of father retreated to depths. Brain felt on fire. She appeared wholly feminine and angelic. **Love transformed him**: Vexed about dust on boots, walked like madman, ate and spoke excitedly. She bent upon Marius all reveries of virginal and passionate eye. M. Leblanc noticed something, often rose when Marius arrived, moved to adjacent bench, stared intently. **Escalation (Spring Year 4)**: Found handkerchief on bench—white, fine, perfumed, marked U. F. Marius thought "Ursule!" Kissed it, placed on heart during day, beneath lips at night. **Leg incident and jealousy**: May breeze lifted dress to height of garter. A leg of exquisite shape appeared. Marius exasperated and furious. Girl hastily thrust down dress with divinely troubled motion. Harsh and capricious jealousy of flesh awakened in his heart. When she passed, Marius darted sullen and ferocious glance. She gave slight backward movement: "Well, what is the matter?" Veteran in Louis XV uniform bearing soldier's cross crossed walk; Marius perceived satisfied air, struck him aged cynic addressed him fraternal wink. **Marius reached paroxysm of jealousy.** "Perhaps he was there! Perhaps he saw!"

**Disappearance and rediscovery (Summer-Autumn Year 4)**: Summer passed, autumn came. Neither returned to Luxembourg. Fell into black melancholy. Allowed himself taken to ball at Sceaux (September) hoping to find her; did not see her; left friends, returned home on foot alone through night, weary, feverish. **Miraculous rediscovery (Autumn Year 4, afternoon before crisis)**: **Marius perceived girl in Jondrette hovel when she arrived with M. Leblanc.** "It was certainly she. Marius could hardly distinguish her through the luminous vapor which had suddenly spread before his eyes." **Marius shuddered in dismay, felt on brink of bursting into tears.** During entire visit, Marius lived in ecstasy; eyes remained fixed on girl; heart seized and wholly enveloped her. He devoured her with his eyes. Could not believe divine creature was in midst of vile creatures in that monstrous lair. Seemed to him he beheld humming-bird in midst of toads.

**Crisis of conscience (evening, crisis escalating)**: Everything depended on Marius. Unknown to themselves, he held all beings in his hand. If he fired pistol, M. Leblanc saved, Thénardier lost; if he did not fire, M. Leblanc sacrificed. Remorse awaited him either case. What should he choose? Be false to most imperious souvenirs, all solemn vows, most sacred duty, most venerated text? Ignore father's testament or allow perpetration of crime? On one hand heard "his Ursule" supplicating for her father; on other, colonel commending Thénardier to his care. **He felt he was going mad. His knees gave way beneath him.** Had not time for deliberation—scene hastening to catastrophe. **He was on verge of swooning.** **Marius regained some measure of control. Last possibility of doubt vanished. Certainly was Thénardier of the will.** Marius shuddered at reproach of ingratitude directed against his father, which he was on point of so fatally justifying. **His perplexity was redoubled.** Critical realization: father once saved by Thénardier at Waterloo—sergeant rescued colonel. Yet M. Leblanc now victim of Thénardier's ambush. Moral obligation to both: honor father's will (protect Thénardier) AND prevent crime against innocent man and Cosette's father. **Crisis of conscience at absolute peak.**

**Current state (evening)**: A sort of horrible fascination held him nailed to post. Almost incapable of movement or reflection, annihilated by abominable things viewed at such close quarters. He waited, in hope of some incident, no matter of what nature, since he could not collect his thoughts and did not know upon what course to decide.

## The Ruffians and Thénardier's Gang
**Seven "chimney-builders" and associates**: Masked or covered with paste—made charcoal-burners, negroes, or demons. Stupid and gloomy air. Perpetrated crime like bit of work, tranquilly, without wrath or mercy, with sort of ennui. Crowded together in one corner like brutes, remained silent.

**Thénardier woman's frustration**: Wife returned from reconnaissance. "That old fellow has duped you! You are too good, you see! If it had been me, I'd have chopped the beast in four quarters to begin with! And if he had acted ugly, I'd have boiled him alive! He would have been obliged to speak, and say where the girl is, and where he keeps his shiners! That's the way I should have managed matters! People are perfectly right when they say that men are a deal stupider than women! Nobody at No. 17. It's nothing but a big carriage gate! No Monsieur Fabre in the Rue Saint-Dominique! And after all that racing and fee to the coachman and all! I spoke to both the porter and the portress, a fine, stout woman, and they know nothing about him!"

## M. Leblanc's Extraordinary Act (Crisis Turning Point)
**Before seven men could collect senses**: M. Leblanc bent down into fireplace, stretched out hand to brazier, straightened himself up. Now **brandished above his head the red-hot chisel, which emitted threatening glow**—almost free and in formidable attitude. Thénardier, female Thénardier, and ruffians huddled in amazement at extremity of hovel, stared in stupefaction.

**Means of escape**: Prisoner had coin piece on person when searched; contrived to conceal it in hand; having right hand free, unscrewed it and used as saw to cut cords fastening him—explaining faint noise and almost imperceptible movements Marius had observed.

**Marius's response**: Reeled in utter horror. Very ruffians shuddered. Hardly muscle of old man's face contracted. While red-hot iron sank into smoking wound, **impassive and almost august, he fixed on Thénardier his beautiful glance, in which there was no hatred, and where suffering vanished in serene majesty.**

## English Provincial Towns: Mundane Activities and Births
**Pelde Stenson and Davus Stenworth/related family circle**: Daily activities: sorting old letters by candlelight, mending torn sleeves, scrubbing steps, humming childhood tunes. Dalis (daughter) born; predicted rain wrongly; laughed at stories nobody else found funny. Havus laughed at story nobody else found funny; counted coins twice and came up penny short; apprenticed anew and became weaver. Yera Stenworth, Nerine Prydenridge, Luvie Prydenridge, Isric Thornmere, Islan, Zavus Prydenridge, Vesmira Thornmere, Wenelle Lindmere (gave up idleness, took work as chandler). General conversations: weather, harvest, lame horse, rain, river up, price of salt. **Kadrek went along to live in Wilholt. Only daughter of Zalis Corrley left Torton and settled in Wilholt.** Baker's boy late again; line at oven grew long. Almanac read aloud (mispronounced saints).
